name: M61 Cepheid 124
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M61 that pulsates every 68.2 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 68.17 d in Markham et al. (2026), ApJ 1000, 78, Appendix A (the table of the final Cepheid candidates in NGC 4303), ID 124: P 68.17 +/- 3.81 d; not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 68.17 d in Markham et al. (2026), ApJ 1000, 78, Appendix A (the table of the final Cepheid candidates in NGC 4303), ID 124: P 68.17 +/- 3.81 d; not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M61, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261...21Y; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M61 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 16,988,675 pc (src/objects/m61-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 16,990,000 pc, inclination 23.5 deg, line of nodes 312.4 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Leroy et al. (2021), PHANGS-ALMA, ApJS 257, 43, table of galaxies, row NGC4303: distance 16.99 ± 3.02 Mpc, from the compilation of Anand et al. (2021) (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJS/257/43)

position.credit: Markham et al. (2026), ApJ 1000, 78, Appendix A (the table of the final Cepheid candidates in NGC 4303), ID 124

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M61, 17.0 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 68.2 days.
text.introduction: Markham et al. (2026) list it among the 130 Cepheid candidates Hubble found in the galaxy, pulsating every 68.2 days.
text.locator: Appendix A, ID 124: P; abstract (the 130 candidates)

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M61 is not measured
